name: Borosil Renewables Ltd
title: Borosil Renewables Ltd - 502219 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

summary.headline: Borosil Renewables Q1 FY27 standalone sales rose 53% YoY to INR405.69 crore and EBITDA to INR142 crore (35% margin), helped by a fuel surcharge.
summary.overview: Standalone sales were INR405.69 crore, up 53% YoY from INR332.26 crore, while EBITDA rose to INR142 crore at 35% of sales versus 27.9% a year ago. Average ex-factory realisation rose to INR160.30 per sq m from INR150.20 in Q4 FY26, including a INR9.50 fuel surcharge introduced from 10 March 2026 after the West Asia war raised fuel costs. Management said the surcharge is now being cut as fuel prices ease, and that the 600 TPD furnace expansion is on track for commissioning in Q1 FY27-end (January to March 2027). Reported PAT of about INR169 crore in Q4 FY26 was inflated by a INR75 crore tax write-back, so the sequential PAT comparison is not like-for-like.

segments.name: Solar glass (core, standalone)
segments.commentary: Plants run at full capacity of 1,000 TPD; realisation INR160.30 per sq m, with EBITDA margin above 33% for the fourth straight quarter. Top 10 customers are about 65-68% of volume.

segments.name: Overseas subsidiaries (German step-downs)
segments.commentary: No revenue in Q1 FY27 and an EBITDA loss of INR0.84 crore, against INR14.32 crore revenue and INR23.24 crore loss a year earlier. Investment written off in the books after the court administrator indicated no recovery.

segments.name: Rooftop solar (new)
segments.commentary: Early-stage on-grid residential kit (module, inverter, battery) sold as a system. Q1 revenue about INR1.3 crore against an internal FY27 target of about INR36 crore; EBITDA margin expected in single digits, versus 30-35% for glass.

guidance_outlook: 600 TPD expansion at the existing site: construction targeted by December 2026, commissioning January to March 2027 (SG4 and SG5, about one month apart). Management says revenue should be modelled from 1 April 2027, though the internal target is 1 March.
Once the 600 TPD is commissioned, sales are expected to rise about 60%, adding about INR80-85 crore of quarterly EBITDA at current run-rate and prices.
Realisation to fall as the INR9.50 fuel surcharge is passed back to customers; management says cost declines should offset this, so profit is not expected to be affected.

Management declined to give a formal guidance but said it expects to continue at similar revenue and EBITDA levels if conditions hold; expects extra profitability this year because prices were at full levels all year.
Ambition to grow from about INR2,500 crore to at least INR4,000 crore revenue in 3-4 years after March 2027; next expansion decision expected within about 6 months.
capex_capacity: Current capacity 1,000 TPD; expansion of 600 TPD at existing location takes it to 1,600 TPD, with the expansion fully funded per management.

Furnace SG1 and SG2 refurbishment: timing not fixed, possibly Q4 FY27 to Q2 FY28, likely after SG4/SG5 are commissioned. A rebuild needs about 75 days of shutdown plus 15 days to restart, so about 90 days with no output from the furnace being rebuilt.
Any further capacity beyond the 600 TPD expansion would be a new building and facility, sized at 600 or 1,200 TPD, and not an add-on to the current layout.
Domestic solar glass capacity expected to reach 7,700 TPD by March 2027 (about 51 GW), against about 2,600 TPD (18 GW) today and about 11,000 TPD demand for 62 GW of module requirement.

Module capacity in India is 203 GW; solar cell capacity is 30 GW, expected to rise to 75 GW by 2027 under ALMM-2 (effective 1 June 2026). ALMM-3 for ingot and wafer starts 28 June, with about 50 GW expected by 2029.
demand_pricing: Management says domestic industry supplies only about 25% of demand; even at 7,700 TPD, supply would cover only 75%, so pricing is expected to hold, with import-parity pricing as the reference.
Exports to the US are very small and in niche applications; the company is focused on the domestic market.
A significant portion of new domestic capacity is captive, so the open-market supply gain is limited, according to management.
Management expects module makers to consolidate over the next 1-1.5 years because module capacity far exceeds requirement; Mono PERC players and those without cell supply may drop volumes.
CVD of 9.71% on solar glass imports from Malaysia extended for five more years from 2 June 2026, on top of anti-dumping duties on China and Vietnam since December 2024.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PAT fall from INR169 crore in Q4 to INR87 crore in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 FY26 PAT included a INR75 crore tax write-back tied to the write-off of the German subsidiary investment (INR325 crore provision). Excluding it, performance was not inferior.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital days rose from 34 to 152; is that right?
qa_highlights.answer: Management disputed the 152-day figure, saying working capital is about 60 days, with a slight rise from stores inventory.

qa_highlights.question: Will domestic prices fall as capacity grows to 7,700 TPD?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said demand is robust, with domestic supply covering only about 25% now, and that pricing is anchored to import parity, so no pricing challenge is foreseen.

qa_highlights.question: What is the rooftop solar business worth?
qa_highlights.answer: Internal FY27 revenue target is about INR36 crore, Q1 revenue about INR1.3 crore, with single-digit EBITDA margins because it is a trading-style solution business.

qa_highlights.question: Any equity raise or debt plan?
qa_highlights.answer: The current expansion is fully funded. Future projects will be funded from internal cash, with some debt if the project is large. No near-term equity raise is planned.

qa_highlights.question: How is the gross margin around 80% calculated?
qa_highlights.answer: Management put gross margin at about 78% on a manufacturing-cost basis, with raw material at about 23-24% of sales, and said margin volatility is not expected.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost of the SG1 patch repair and the volume effect of furnace rebuilds?
qa_highlights.answer: A four-day patch on one furnace cost about INR3 crore in lost output. A full rebuild would shut the furnace for about 90 days, causing a volume loss in the year it happens.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tax rate for the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 25.2% should be assumed for the full year.

risks_watch: Fuel-surcharge unwind: the INR9.50 per sq m surcharge is being reduced as fuel prices ease, so realisation could fall from INR160.30 even with stable costs. Management says the cost decline offsets it.
Commissioning risk: the 600 TPD expansion (SG4, SG5) must be commissioned by March 2027, with revenue only from April 2027. Any delay pushes the 60% volume uplift later.
Furnace SG1/SG2 rebuild: about 90 days of lost output per furnace, timing not fixed (Q4 FY27 to Q2 FY28); this could reduce FY28 volumes against the 1,600 TPD capacity.
Customer concentration: top 10 customers are about 65-68% of volume, and module consolidation could affect volumes.
Capacity additions in domestic glass (to 7,700 TPD by March 2027) could pressure prices, though management expects supply to stay short.
Rooftop solar and the overseas subsidiaries are small and early, with unclear profitability; the call gave no segment-level data.
Management declined to comment on press reports of a strategic investment. Next-phase project choice (glass furnace or adjacent business) is due in about 5-6 months.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operations and demand, with management stressing full plant utilisation and a robust domestic market. It was evasive on guidance, declining to give formal numbers, and on the strategic investment press reports. Defensive on the PAT comparison, which it attributed to a one-off tax write-back.
key_quotes: I'm happy to inform that we were able to operate the plants at full capacity despite disruption in fuel supplies and the prices led by war in West Asia.
So if you really remove that INR75 crores, the performance is not inferior.
So our expansion is exactly 60% of the current capacity. And we are assuming the prices to remain same way.

adds.what: 600 TPD furnace expansion at existing Borosil Renewables site (1,000 TPD to 1,600 TPD)

growth.why: Management guides roughly +60% sales and EBITDA once the 600 TPD expansion (1,000 to 1,600 TPD) is commissioned in Jan-Mar 2027, backed by work under way, though realisation falls as the INR9.50 fuel surcharge is withdrawn and the furnace rebuilds later will cost about 90 days of output.
